title: Inherited populate_by_name leaked into subclasses because ConfigWrapper mutated model_config
answers: child model populate_by_name=False still accepts field names
model_config contains validate_by_name/validate_by_alias I never set
why is my ConfigDict mutated after defining a model
body:
Symptom: a subclass setting `populate_by_name=False` still validated by field name when its parent had `populate_by_name=True`. `Model.model_config` (and a user's ConfigDict passed to a TypeAdapter, dataclass, validate_call or validate_arguments) also showed `validate_by_alias`/`validate_by_name` keys the user never set.
Root cause: `ConfigWrapper.core_config` in pydantic/_internal/_config.py wrote the derived `validate_by_*` keys straight into `config_dict`. That dict is the user's own object and it gets merged into subclasses, so the derived `validate_by_name=True` beat the child's explicit `populate_by_name`.
Fix pattern: work out derived settings in a non-mutating `_build_effective_config` (returns `{**config, ...}`) and store the result on `ConfigWrapper.effective_config`. `prepare_config` now copies any dict it receives.
Constraints: user-visible change. `model_config` now shows only what the user declared. Tests that assert derived keys in `model_config` must check validation behaviour instead (see tests/test_config.py:test_dynamic_default).
applies: pydantic config handling: ConfigWrapper, model_config inheritance, alias/name validation settings
